section.title: Software Engineering Core
section.label: Section Two
section.description: The working vocabulary of building and running software — algorithms, architecture, concurrency, databases, security and the field's durable jargon. Definitions are written to be substitutable, and the idioms carry the origin story only where it is actually documented.

definitions.text: the future cost incurred by choosing an expedient implementation now instead of a sounder one, paid back as extra effort on every later change.
definitions.example: Shipping the prototype as-is bought us a quarter and left three months of technical debt.

definitions.text: the accumulated backlog of deferred cleanup, upgrades and documentation that a codebase carries as a measurable liability.
definitions.example: The team reserves one sprint in five for technical debt.

entries.etymology: Coined by Ward Cunningham in a 1992 OOPSLA experience report, extending the financial sense of debt: shipping imperfect code is borrowing against future velocity, and the interest is the extra work every subsequent change costs.

citations.label: Cunningham, W. (1992). The WyCash Portfolio Management System.
